source: Sivasubramanian (2012) PhD thesis, Univ. of Arizona (hdl:10150/228514), Fig. 5.1 (PDF p.136): N-factor curves for axisymmetric waves (kc=0) from the low-amplitude DNS wave-packet simulation on a sharp 7-deg cone at Mach 6 (BAM6QT). This thesis is the parent of, and the linear regime of, Sivasubramanian & Fasel (2015) JFM 768:175-218. Verbatim: the most-amplified axisymmetric wave reaches N~9.5; it has F=1.071e-5 (f*~210 kHz) and is the highest-N wave in the computational domain. Cross-checked vs the BAM6QT design review arXiv:2509.10411 (sharp-cone TM edge Me~5.6 / cone Me~5.5; second-mode N 'around 8 at end of cone, almost 9 at end of flare', 'N>10 for low-noise environment').

conditions.geometry: sharp circular cone, 7 deg half-angle, length 0.5 m, nose radius 0.05 mm (sharp), zero incidence (Mangler path)
conditions.formulation: spatial 2nd mode (L* scale, lambda_mu_ratio=1.2), cone Mangler N=int 6 sigma_L dR_eq, clip_negative (envelope from lower neutral point)
conditions.freestream_BAM6QT: M_inf=6, T0=430 K, T_inf=52.4 K, V_inf=871 m/s, Re/m~10.5e6/m (thesis) / 11.2e6/m (design review), Tw=300 K, p0~1043 kPa
conditions.edge_provenance: Taylor-Maccoll solve (7 deg, M_inf=6, gamma=1.4); shock angle beta=11.94 deg. Cross-check: arXiv:2509.10411 reports cone M_e~5.5 / TM M_e~5.6 for a 5-deg cone; our larger 7-deg cone -> lower edge Mach 5.36, physically consistent.
conditions.transverse_curvature: OMITTED (Mangler scope); valid since delta << r_local = s*sin(7deg) over the matched window
conditions.x_star_nondimensionalization: x* is the DIMENSIONAL AXIAL distance in METERS along the cone axis (thesis quotes x*=0.138 m, 0.250 m, 0.58 m, etc.). pyMack works in surface distance s along the ray; for a sharp cone s = x*/cos(7deg) ~= 1.0075 x*. Computational domain x*0=0.1 m (inflow) to x*L=0.6 m (outflow); 0.5 m physical cone, buffer beyond.
conditions.domain_matched_window: thesis Fig. 5.1 x* axial 0.30->0.59 m -> surface s=302->594 mm -> R_eq=sqrt(Re_s/3)=1194->1674; N integrated from the lower neutral point (x*~0.30 m, where sigma first >0; clip_negative anchors N=0 there, matching the thesis A_0 reference).

quantity: second-mode peak-N frequency (kHz) and peak linear N-factor on the sharp cone, integrated over the SAME physical extent as thesis Fig. 5.1 (lower neutral point -> domain end)

metrics.headline: f: 210 kHz EXACT match (pyMack peak-N at 205 kHz; N=8.05 at the thesis 210 kHz). N: pyMack domain-matched 8.0-8.1 vs thesis 9.5 -> ~15% short (Mangler self-similar BL under-predicts the back-half DNS growth).
metrics.design_review_cross_check: arXiv:2509.10411: second-mode N ~8 at end of cone, ~9 at end of flare, >10 low-noise; brackets thesis 9.5 and validates N~8-10 magnitude on this cone

verdict_reason: PRIOR-VERSION ERROR CORRECTED. The previous verdict used loose secondary values (peak N~7-8, most-amplified band 220-280 kHz) citing the JFM paper generically; the 220-280 kHz band actually came from a different Reynolds condition in the design review, not from this case. The ORIGINAL source -- Sivasubramanian (2012) PhD thesis Fig. 5.1, the linear parent of Sivasubramanian & Fasel (2015) JFM 768 -- states VERBATIM that the most-amplified axisymmetric wave (kc=0) reaches N~9.5 and has F=1.071e-5 (f*~210 kHz). The benchmark is therefore peak N~9.5 at f~210 kHz, NOT 7-8 / 220-280 kHz. DOMAIN-MATCHED RE-INTEGRATION: the thesis integrates N=ln(A/A0) from each wave's lower neutral point over its x* domain (axial 0.30->0.59 m, into the x*L=0.6 m buffer). Mapping that physical extent to pyMack's surface s=x*/cos(7deg) and R_eq=sqrt(Re_s/3) with the same Taylor-Maccoll edge state, and integrating from the lower neutral point (clip_negative, matching A0), pyMack's peak-N frequency is 205 kHz (N=8.11) with N=8.05 evaluated at the thesis 210 kHz. FREQUENCY: 210 vs 210 kHz is an EXACT match (2.4% if read at pyMack's own 205 kHz peak) -- pyMack independently reproduces F=1.071e-5 as the most-amplified frequency. N-FACTOR: pyMack 8.0-8.1 vs thesis 9.5 is ~15% short. The shape tracks the thesis well through x*~0.50 m (pyMack 6.5 vs ~6.6) but the self-similar Blasius/Mangler local growth rate decays faster than the cone DNS in the back half (x*>0.47 m: pyMack sigma falls from 4.3e-3 to 0.6e-3), so the last ~1.4 of N is not accumulated. This is the expected signature of omitting transverse curvature and the real non-similar cone mean flow. The domain-matched N (8.05) is a clear improvement over the prior loose-window 7.06, and is cross-validated by the BAM6QT design review (N~8 at end of cone, ~9 at end of flare, >10 low-noise -- bracketing 9.5). VERDICT = acceptable: frequency agrees exactly, N sits right at the 15% boundary with a bounded, physically-understood Mangler/self-similar deficit; no topology/mode mismatch (clean discrete second mode, single growth lobe, monotone N from the lower neutral point).
